record.paper_title: Mathematical open problems in Projected Entangled Pair States
record.original_question: Suppose two local tensors A and B define exactly the same projected entangled pair state on every L by L torus, meaning the PEPS generated by A equals the PEPS generated by B for all system sizes L. What local relation between A and B characterizes this equality of PEPS?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Fix integers $d, D \ge 1$. A local PEPS tensor on the square lattice is a four-index tensor 
$$A \in \mathbb{C}^{d} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{D} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{D} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{D} \otimes \mathbb{C}^{D},$$
with one "physical" index of dimension $d$ and four "virtual" indices of dimension $D$ (assigned to the directions up, right, down, left). For each integer $L \ge 1$, the PEPS on the $L\times L$ torus generated by $A$ is the vector
$$|\Psi_L(A)\rangle \in \bigl(\mathbb{C}^d\bigr)^{\otimes L^2}$$
obtained by placing a copy of $A$ at every vertex of the $L\times L$ periodic square lattice and contracting each pair of virtual indices that meet along an edge (with periodic boundary conditions in both directions).

Two local tensors $A$ and $B$ (with the same physical dimension $d$ but possibly different virtual dimensions $D_A, D_B$) are said to generate the same PEPS on every torus if
$$|\Psi_L(A)\rangle = |\Psi_L(B)\rangle \quad \text{for every } L \ge 1.$$

Problem. Find an explicit local algebraic relation between $A$ and $B$ that characterizes the property of generating the same PEPS on every $L \times L$ torus. That is, give necessary and sufficient conditions, formulated purely in terms of the tensors $A$ and $B$ themselves (for example, via gauges, similarities on the virtual level, or limits of such transformations), under which $|\Psi_L(A)\rangle = |\Psi_L(B)\rangle$ for all $L$. In particular, decide whether this equivalence is characterized by a single, finite, locally checkable relation, and whether the resulting decision problem is decidable.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work (notably the "minimal canonical form" framework, arXiv:2209.14358) established a Fundamental Theorem characterizing when two PEPS tensors define the same state on every closed surface: they must be gauge-equivalent up to limits, and this problem is decidable. However, restricting equality to periodic rectangular lattices (tori only) is known to be undecidable in general, and no clean local algebraic characterization for that case is known. Thus the torus-only version remains essentially open, while the broader "all geometries" version is settled.

status_evidence.title: The minimal canonical form of a tensor network
status_evidence.snippet: Two tensors have the same minimal canonical forms iff they are gauge equivalent up to taking limits, iff they give the same quantum state for any geometry; this problem is decidable, in contrast to the undecidability for PEPS on grids.
status_evidence.claim: Equality on all surfaces is characterized by gauge equivalence up to limits and is decidable; equality on rectangular grids/tori is undecidable.

status_evidence.title: MPS and PEPS: Concepts, Symmetries, and Theorems
status_evidence.snippet: Fundamental theorems for PEPS state conditions under which two tensors generate the same state, with known limitations on rectangular lattices.
status_evidence.claim: A local-relation characterization for torus-only equality is not fully established.
